So that I know better your background, and for the final test that try to签签到。Adjust your background.〔待核 U001：此处英中混合及句法不清〕 So, I will talk with the technology professors〔待核 U002〕 and see how to make things suitable for all of you, so that the final tests can suit your background and ability to learn new concepts but starting from what you know already. OK?你能写中文吗？〔待核 U003：模型对此处给出不同英文，不能据上下文判定语言〕

Any any questions or anything that you would like me to repeat or better explain about what we said yesterday? Feel free to ask for clarification or if you missed anything, please ask. Anything that you would like to hear again? OK, so, then let me ask you, just to see if we are all good so far.

So, when we have a transmitter and a receiver of information, how can we transfer information data from a transmitter to a receiver? How can we do that?

How can we impress information bits on the signal electromagnetic wave that travels from transmitter to receiver? Modulation. Okay, but I know you have got an ICT background. Okay, thanks.〔补回 A001，待核；说话人未重新识别〕
So, modulation, modulation is the operation that allow us to impress bits on a signal, right? And we can do that by changing amplitude or frequency or phase of the signal, OK?

Also, we said at the receiver, when the power of the received signal is too low compare to noise interference, we may make mistakes, and we said there are techniques to help the receiver to receive correctly the information. A possible family group of techniques is the forward error correction codes, and we made the example of the repetition code, very simple. And it's what we do, we humans do, to repeat information whenever the receiver is not able to understand correctly.

The second type of technique that we are going to discuss today is ARQ, automatic retransmission request. OK, this is what we are going to explain in a minute, but what we already said yesterday is that in this second case we handle bits grouped into packets. OK? So, we do not look at the single bits, but we look at a group of bits that are carried into a packet, and the packet we said is like a message, an email that we send, right? And the single bits are like the letters that we write in the message, in the email message. Okay?

So, we send a packet from a transmitter to a receiver. So, we can think of it in our daily life as an email message. And we let this packet get a header in front. That means like when we write an email, we said we are going to add our address, and of course, the address of the destination. Right? So that kind of information is the header of the email [00:08:07] message that we write, and the same holds here, we have the base, the information〔待核 U004〕 that is included in the payload. And then we have the header that carries the so called control information. Examples are the sender's address and the destination's address. OK.

Now, in this header, there may be other control information on top of the transmitters' and receivers' address.〔补回 A002，待核〕

Now, in a ARQ techniques, what we do is given an transmitter and a receiver, and given a packet that the transmitter sends to the receiver, we are going to, to include in the packet header at the transmitter a digest of the payload. That means a summary of the payload. That is called CRC code. OK, so, it's still a kind of a code, it's called CRC code, and it is a digest. Sorry, let me write a simple answer for it.〔待核 U005〕

This is a digest of the payload. OK, a digest summary of the information bits. This CRC, this digest of the information bits is included by the transmitter into the packet header, and then the transmitter transmits everything, the payload and the header, to the intended receiver. OK?

The intended receiver will try to demodulate what it receives. So, to extract all the bits. OK. Assume that the header of the packet is always received correctly at the receiver.〔推定 C005〕 Let's make this assumption. So first, it demodulates the header〔推定 C006〕 and extracts the CRC that was computed by the transmitter.

OK? So, the receiver demodulates first the CRC〔推定 C007〕 that was computed at the transmitter, and then it demodulates the payload, the information bits.

Now, after that, the receiver itself computes the CRC, the digest of the information bits of the payload that it has demodulated. OK, so, based on what it understood from the payload that it has received, it computes its own CRC. OK, so we have a value of CRC computed at the receiver that is a digest of what the receiver has understood from the thing that it has received〔推定 C011〕.

OK, now, at the receiver, we have both the CRC that was transmitted by the transmitter, and the CRC that the receiver has computed locally. If they are the same, if they are equal, if they are the same, then the receiver says I received everything correctly.

Okay. If instead, the two values are different, then the receiver〔补回 A003，待核〕 [00:14:27] says, I failed, I could not receive the packet correctly. OK, so the packet transmission failed.

OK, now, that said, when we apply ARQ, there might be different〔补回 A004，待核〕 [00:15:03] ARQ techniques that one can implement, but we will look only at one of them, that is the simplest ARQ technique. And this is called stop and wait. Ok, this is the only ARQ technique that we are going to discuss. How does the stop and wait work?

OK, how does the stop and wait technique work? As we said, the transmitter transmits the packet payload plus header. In the header, there is the CRC computed by the transmitter. The receiver demodulates the header, and we assume that it always demodulates the header correctly. Therefore, it extracts the CRC computed by the transmitter.〔补回 A005，含推定，待核〕 Then, as we said, it demodulates the payload of the packet〔推定 C016〕, and based on what the receiver got, the modulated〔待核 U006〕 computes its own summary of the payload, and this is the CRC computed at the receiver.

And then it checks whether these two values are equal or different. If they are equal, then he says, I have received the packet correctly. And at this point, he will send back an control packet, that is called acknowledgment. So, it will send back an ACK, an acknowledgment to the transmitter.
The acknowledgment is a control packet. It means that it does not carry any useful user information. It just says, I received your packet correctly. OK, that's the meaning of acknowledgment.

When the transmitter receives the acknowledgment from the receiver, it understands that its packet was successful. So, he's happy with that, and he will proceed with the next packet transmission, if it has something more to drive〔待核 U007〕.

If instead, as the receiver, we find that these two values are different, then the receiver will say the transmission of the packet failed, and it will not send back anything. OK, so no acknowledgment in this case.

The receiver〔待核 U008：源文与模型均如此，按流程此处可能为transmitter的口误或误识〕, therefore, in this case does not receive any acknowledgment, and it understands that its transmission failed. OK, there is a timeout, if the receiver〔待核 U009：同上角色问题〕 does not receive any ACK after this time, it says, oh, my packet failed. And what it will do is to transmit the same packet again, and we repeat the procedure. So, it sends the packet again, the receiver receives the signal, it demodulates the header first,〔推定 C018〕 [00:20:25] gets the CRC computed by the transmitter, and demodulates again the payload, computes the CRC locally.〔推定 C019〕

Again he compares the two values, and if they are the same, OK, then he says, well, now I understand I received the packet correctly, and sends back ACK. If they are again different, it would say the transmission failed again. And it will not send back anything.

So, the transmitter after a timeout understands that its packet transmission failed, and will try again, and so on, and so forth, till we either get the packet transmission successful, or we reach a maximum number of attempts, after which the transmitter gives up and discards the packet. Ok?

So, this technique is called stop and wait, because the transmitter, after having transmitted the packet, will stop and wait for the acknowledgment from the receiver.

If it receives the acknowledgment, fine, we can proceed with a new packet transmission.

Instead, if the packet transmission fails, the transmitter will repeat the transmission, OK? This process of repeating the transmission, as we said, goes on till a maximum number of times. Okay, we do not continue to infinity, we stop at a certain point,〔补回 A007，待核〕 [00:23:04] and if the transmitter cannot transmit the packet successfully after a maximum number of attempts, it just discards the packet.

OK, now, as we said, this kind of techniques are called ARQ, right? Automatic retransmission request, and now we understand also why they are called automatic retransmission request, because the receiver by not sending the acknowledgment will implicitly request a retransmission by the receiver.〔推定 C023，末尾角色待核〕

OK, so, the coverage of Wi-Fi, as said yesterday, is relatively small, I would say medium. Indeed, Wi-Fi is a technology to provide the so called wireless local area networks. OK, so, to provide connectivity to users locally, to implement the so called local area networks.

So, we already said that Wi-Fi is a technology to implement wireless local area networks to provide connectivity to wireless users. As we said, this is a standard also. The technology is specified by the IEEE 802.11 standard.

And the standard of Wi-Fi defines two layers of the protocol stack, the physical layer and the MAC layer.

Now, I know that you have different backgrounds, so let me just recall what is a protocol stack. OK, so let's consider the Wi-Fi card that we have in our phone. Okay, there is a Wi-Fi card inside. What is this wi fi card? The Wi-Fi card is an device, a drawing device〔待核 U011〕 that implements different functions.

Some functions are used to transmit the signal. OK, so, it is these functions are called physical, physical layer, physical layer〔补回 A009，待核〕 [00:38:05] functions. Why? Because they are used to physically transmit the signal.

On top of these functions, we have the so called MAC layer.

The MAC layer, MAC means medium access control. The MAC layer groups those functions that are used by the Wi-Fi card to understand when you can send a packet.

whatever you use as an application.

And a photo is made of pixels, right? They are data, they can be encoded into bits. OK, so now we have these bits that correspond to a photo. These bits are grouped into packets, so we have the packets generated by the application.

Okay, now each of these packets〔补回 A011，待核〕 [00:41:13] need to be uploaded, right? Because you want to upload your picture. So, these packets need to be transferred over the access point, and then from the access point to the internet.

Okay, so then the picture will be stored, for example, in a repository. So the goal is to transfer the application packets〔补回 A012，待核〕 [00:41:55] to the access point, and then to the internet.

What Wi-Fi will do is to transfer these packets from your Wi-Fi card in your phone to the access point. That's what Wi-Fi does. OK, so, Wi-Fi acts at these layers. Hmm.

So, to let these packets be transmitted to the access point, inside your phone, inside your phone, these packets need to be moved from this application to these other layers of this stack [00:42:53] of layers, okay, till they reach the MAC layer, and then they go down to the physical layer. This is Wi-Fi, and then they are transmitted over the air to the access point.

Just as an example, these intermediate layers between the application and your Wi-Fi layers, let's call them like Wi-Fi layers,〔补回 A013，含推定，待核〕 [00:43:33] they include TCP, if you have heard of TCP, or IP, if you heard of IP, otherwise don't worry, OK? OK, but just to say that between your application layer that generates the photo, and where Wi-Fi operates inside your phone or inside your laptop, there are other layers, OK? The packet generated by the application goes down through these layers inside your phone till it reaches the MAC layer.

Then we see how the Wi-Fi MAC layer works, and then the MAC layer sends the packet to the physical layer, and then the physical layer transmits physically the bits. How? By impressing the bits into the electromagnetic wave, and then travels through the air and goes to the antenna. OK, so what we discuss yesterday, modulation is performed here at the physical layer. And then the physical layer generates this electromagnetic signal that is actually transmitted through the antenna that is here at the physical layer. And then through the antenna we send the signal. OK? Wi-Fi [00:45:53] specifies how these two layers work.
